key_policy: Permanent local letters, independent of display order. Append new keys; retire rather than reuse. A changed requirement needs a new key.

focuses.source_text:
Know the definition and understand the purpose of computational

thinking.

elements.requirement: Purpose and appropriate use: computational thinking.

focuses.source_text: Know when to use computational thinking.

elements.requirement: Choose when computational thinking is appropriate.
elements.topic: Choose when computational thinking is appropriate.

focuses.source_text:
Know and understand the benefits and drawbacks of using

computational thinking.

Know the components of computational thinking:

- decomposition
- pattern recognition
- abstraction
- algorithmic design.

Know and understand the benefits and drawbacks of using the

components of computational thinking.
Know and understand the purpose of decomposition.

Know the tasks of decomposition:

- identify the main features of a problem
- characterise each identified feature
- break problems down into smaller, more manageable parts
- break solutions down into smaller, more manageable parts.

elements.requirement: Identify the main features of a problem.
elements.topic: Identify the main features of a problem.

elements.requirement: Break a problem into manageable parts.
elements.topic: Break a problem into manageable parts.

elements.requirement: Break a solution into manageable parts.
elements.topic: Break a solution into manageable parts.

focuses.source_text: Be able to use decomposition for problem solving.

Know and understand methods to represent decomposition:

- block diagrams
- information flow diagrams
- flowcharts
- code
- written descriptions.

elements.requirement: Understand the representation: information flow diagrams.

focuses.source_text: Be able to use the methods to represent decomposition.

elements.requirement: Use to represent decomposition: block diagrams.
Use to represent decomposition: information flow diagrams.
Use to represent decomposition: written descriptions.

focuses.source_text: Know and understand the purpose of pattern recognition.

Be able to use pattern recognition for problem solving:

- find and interpret trends and similarities within and between problems
    and processes
- find and interpret common features between a given problem and
    existing solutions
- make predictions and assumptions based on identified patterns.

elements.requirement: Interpret trends and similarities within and between problems and processes.
elements.topic: Interpret trends and similarities within and between problems and processes.

elements.requirement: Identify common features with existing solutions.
elements.topic: Identify common features with existing solutions.

elements.requirement: Make predictions and assumptions from patterns.
elements.topic: Make predictions and assumptions from patterns.

focuses.source_text: Know and understand the purpose of abstraction.

Know and understand the tasks of abstraction:

- identify information that is needed
- filter out unnecessary details
- hide details of internal workings.

Be able to use abstraction:

- what inputs are needed
- what the expected outputs and outcomes are
- things that will vary
- things that will remain constant
- key actions the solution must perform
- repeated processes the solution will perform.
Be able to use abstraction in problem solving.

Understand the interrelationships between components of computational

thinking and make judgements about the suitability of using the
components in digital software development.

elements.requirement: Judge suitability of computational-thinking components for a problem.
elements.topic: Judge suitability of computational-thinking components for a problem.

focuses.source_text:
Know the definition and understand the characteristics and purpose

of algorithms.

Know and understand that algorithms can be expressed in:

- flowcharts:
  - terminators
  - processes
  - sub-processes
  - decisions
  - inputs/outputs
  - arrows
  - labels
- written descriptions using hierarchical markers to indicate sequence
- code (commands in _Appendix 2_ ).

Understand algorithm notation: hierarchical written descriptions.

expressing algorithms in flowcharts.

expressing algorithms in written descriptions.

expressing algorithms in code.

Know and understand actions to control ordering of steps in algorithms:

- sequence
- selection
- iteration.

- five whys
- failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA)
- event tree analysis (ETA)
- actions to take after using root cause analysis:
  - log
  - close
  - escalate to an appropriate manager, specialist or external
       third party.
